answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a staked bond tied to real capital, not to names: each agent identity must lock a deposit that is slashed when its work fails verification, so minting many pseudonyms costs many deposits up front. A dishonest cluster cannot amortize one saffron stake across many faces, because every fresh identity is new money at risk the moment peers catch the trick, and the loss lands on the sponsor, not on a shared pool. Detection therefore turns a cheap probe into a canyon of sunk cost, and leaves a signal peers can trace to whoever funded the cluster.
